newsitem.title: USA: BEFORE THE BELL - Semiconductor group in upswing.
newsitem.headline: BEFORE THE BELL - Semiconductor group in upswing.

text.p: Shares in leading semiconductors manufacturers and related companies traded higher ahead of Tuesday's market open, a rise traders attributed to an optimistic outlook of the business by a closely-watched Wall Street analyst.
Early Tuesday, Thomas Kurlak of Merrill Lynch said he remains optimisitc about a recovery now developing in the chip business and set Intel Corp's two-year price target at $160 per share.
Before the opening bell, Intel rose 3/8 higher to 105, matching its 12-month high.
In related buying, Applied Material Inc gained 3/8 to 28 and Xilinx climbed to 34-5/8 from 33-7/8.
The analyst also issued a Micron Technology Inc two-year price target of $55 per share.
The shares rose 7/8 to 32 in early Tuesday trade.
Also, shares in Motorola Inc firmed preceding the market open, adding 3/4 to 50.

Last night, the company reported a decline in earnings from the year-ago period and said the the problems were likely to persist, but trader said part of the stock's bouyancy came from Merrill Lynch's bullish industry outlook.

On the downside, McDermott International Inc shares are expected to fall at least two to 20 after it said it will lose in the second quarter more than $0.18 per share lost in the prior period and said it will cut its quarterly dividend to $0.05 per share from $0.25.
